CPBC_branching_theorem: A permutation-equivariant set-valued branching relation may contain the full orbit of all k-subsets.
Individual raw histories can then contain exactly k continuing lineage choices.
But CPBC retains all branches; the aggregate source-lineage causal-support union contains every one of the M symmetric incoming lineages whenever any proper-k orbit is admitted.
Therefore raw-history k-splitting is not a unique aggregate causal-support attenuation M->k.
deterministic_theorem: Let the symmetric group S_M permute the M incoming indistinguishable source-tag lineages.
A deterministic permutation-equivariant rule selecting which incoming lineages retain relay-direction causal support must select an S_M-invariant subset.
The only S_M-invariant subsets of a transitive M-element set are the empty set and the full set.
Hence no unique deterministic causal-support transfer can select exactly k of the incoming M lineages for any 0<k<M.
legal_symmetry_preserving_operations: all incoming relay lineages continue: incoming-cohort contribution M
all incoming relay lineages extinguish/settle: incoming-cohort contribution 0
distinguished resident joins while all incoming continue: M->M+1
distinguished resident replaces an all-settled incoming cohort: M->1
no resident relay after incoming settle: M->0
relation_to_positive_family: I_DIVISIBILITY_RELAY_GATE uses only the legal all-incoming-settle plus distinguished-resident 1-or-0 replacement; it never selects one named incoming lineage.
scope: canonical one-resident relay-front grammar with M co-moving incoming source-tag lineages having identical controller-visible signatures and no lineage/tag identity
